    x,
    return_inverse=False,
    return_counts=False,
    axis=None,
    sorted=True,
    size=None,
    fill_value=None,

    arrays and axis-based uniqueness) and the result is converted back to a

    options are applied on top of NumPy's output.

    ndim = ar.ndim

    # `axis is None`, NumPy flattens the input and returns a 1D array, so the
    # values live on axis 0 of the output.

    # (which requires the first-occurrence indices) and `return_counts`.

        ar,
        return_index=True,
        return_inverse=True,
        return_counts=True,
        axis=axis if axis is None else values_axis,
    )

    if not sorted:
        # Reorder the (sorted) unique values by their first appearance in the
        # original input.
        order = np.argsort(first_index, kind="stable")

        counts = counts[order]

                unique_values, np.arange(size), axis=values_axis

            pad = size - n

                    pad_shape = list(unique_values.shape)
                    pad_shape[values_axis] = pad
                    pad_block = np.zeros(pad_shape, dtype=unique_values.dtype)
            else:

                pad_shape[values_axis] = pad
                pad_block = np.full(
                    pad_shape, fill_value, dtype=unique_values.dtype
                )

    if return_counts:
